Hindu Deity Lakshmi Gobinda Jeu ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Deputy Custodian, Enemy Property (now vested property), Government of Bangladesh and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment: 28. In the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record, I am constrained to hold that the learned Courts below. seriously erred in law in dismissing the suit on non-reading and misreading of the material evidence on record and on misconstruction of the important documents in the CS Khatians Exts. 1 and 1(a) and the same has occasioned failure of justice. As the plaintiff has been able to prove its title in the suit land and continuous possession therein, I do not find any reason as to why the suit should not be decreed. In view of the fact that the suit property is a Debutter property of the Deity and there is absolutely no basis for its becoming the secular property of its former Shebait Suresh, the mere recording of the suit property in the name of Suresh in SA khatian is evidently wrong and without any foundation whatsoever and the same cannot affect the plaintiffs right, title and interest in the suit property and any way there is no dispute to the proposition that the CS khatians has a presumption of correctness undersection 103(b) of the Bengal Tenancy Act while the SA khatian has no such presumptive value. The learned Courts below thus evidently erred in law in placing too much reliance on the SA khatians completely ignoring the overwhelming evidence on record to prove that it had no legal foundation and factual basis. For the reasons stated above, I am constrained to hold that the learned Courts below were wrong in passing the impugned judgments on erroneous view of law and on illegal and irrelevant considerations and the same are liable to be set aside in the interest of justice.
